newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Northam, union agree 12.5 pct pay hike.
newsitem.headline: Northam, union agree 12.5 pct pay hike.

text.p: Gold Fields of South Africa's platinum group Northam Platinum announced on Friday it had agreed a 12.5 percent wage increase with the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM).
"Under an agreement signed today, weekly paid surface and underground employees will receive a 12.5 percent increase in their basic pay," the company said in a statement.
The pay increase is effective July 1.
It added that both parties had agreed to enter into discussions on productivity improvements.
Last year, the company reached a settlement with the NUM on a 14 percent increase for union members.
On Thursday, the mine reported a pre-capex loss of 0.63 million rand for the first quarter of the year compared with a first quarter loss of 18.44 million rand.
It said on Thursday that it aimed to raise its milling rate in future in a bid to ensure profitability.
